passages.section: The Ontology of Existence in Madhyasth Darshan
passages.text: Companion to the 29-slide presentation based on §1 of The Ontology of Coexistence (AnalyticMadhyasthDarshan.org). Primary texts cited: Madhyasth Darshan (MVD), Manav Karm Darshan (KD), Samadhanatmak Bhautikvad (SB), Jeevan Vidya – An Introduction (JV), and Adhyatmvad (AVD), and the Hindi Paribhasha Samhita (PS). Translation and edition conventions follow the study; KD section 3 is working English. PS citations use printed pages, eight below the PDF position, in the third edition (2012), printing dated 14 January 2016. The official source collection and page-level references are linked in the study bibliography.

passages.heading: the-ontology-of-existence-in-madhyasth-darshan
passages.section: The Ontology of Existence in Madhyasth Darshan
passages.text: How to use this guide: each slide has three parts. “Delivering the slide” is a complete read-aloud script for live or video-conference delivery, written for a smart audience with no prior Madhyasth Darshan or formal-philosophy background — English first, source terms second; speak it as written (or nearly so). It is mirrored in the PowerPoint notes pane. “Primary-text background” is for pre-session study, not for reading aloud. “Likely questions” is for Q&A preparation.

passages.heading: the-ontology-of-existence-in-madhyasth-darshan
passages.section: The Ontology of Existence in Madhyasth Darshan
passages.text: House conventions: the English translation often prints “Omnipotence” for satta; the study, this guide, and the slides use “Omnipresence” in prose and preserve the translation’s word inside quotations only. Both names point to the same satta. Hindi shunya is rendered “Space.” Where the study flags an open problem, the suggested answers say so plainly — candour about what is and is not established is part of the study’s method. The former four-senses-of-gyan taxonomy is no longer a deck slide; vocabulary discipline lives in the study’s Editorial Notes. The epistemic payoff is the epistemic ladder (slide 24) and realisation (slide 25); presentation, communication, expression, and art connect understanding with conduct (slide 26); method and evidence close the “how known” question (slides 28 and 29).

passages.heading: the-ontology-of-existence-in-madhyasth-darshan
passages.section: The Ontology of Existence in Madhyasth Darshan
passages.text: Three movements: the deck is signposted in the kicker line of each movement’s opening slide — Movement 1 at slide 5 (what is real), Movement 2 at slide 12 (how development proceeds), Movement 3 at slide 17 (from sentience to awakened conduct).

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide
passages.text: Welcome, and thank you for joining.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide
passages.text: You do not need any prior familiarity with Madhyasth Darshan, or with formal philosophy, to follow this session. I will use ordinary English first, and introduce source terms only when they help. Our aim is not persuasion or devotion. It is to examine one coherent account of reality — testing its definitions and internal consistency.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide
passages.text: Madhyasth Darshan — also called Co-existentialism — was propounded by Shri A. Nagraj. The name points to a thesis we will unpack later: order in nature is mediative and inherent, not imposed by an external governor.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide
passages.text: Here is the one claim to hold for the whole talk: existence is coexistence. Reality is the ever-present togetherness of a formless, all-pervasive ground and countless real, bounded units of nature, each saturated in that ground. Everything else — sentience, values, justice, society — unfolds from this picture.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide
passages.text: One word about vocabulary. The published translations often print “Omnipotence” for the ground; the slides and I will say Omnipresence. Same reality, different English label — you will see the translation’s word only inside quotations.

passages.heading: primary-text-background
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background
passages.text: Coverage claims are scoped to the translated corpus (MVD, SB, JV), KD as cited, and the selected Hindi PS definitions identified in this guide. Other Hindi works may develop these subjects further.

passages.heading: primary-text-background
passages.text: “What is evident is that consciousness and matter are inseparably present. Upon examining their fundamental nature, we learn that all of existence is essentially nature (matter) saturated in Omnipotence (consciousness)… existence itself is eternally manifest in the form of coexistence.” — SB, p. 48

passages.heading: primary-text-background
passages.text: Translation convention: the English translation prints “Omnipotence” for satta and “Omnipresence” for vyapak; the study uses “Omnipresence” in analytical prose. Hindi shunya is rendered “Space” — void/emptiness, not physical akasha.

passages.heading: primary-text-background
passages.text: MD’s own title for SB — Samadhanatmak Bhautikvad, Resolution Centred Materialism — signals that the darshan reframes materialism rather than abandoning it (SB, pp. 8, 44).

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience
passages.text: Q: What does “Madhyasth” mean, and why is the darshan named after it? Madhyasth means mediative. MVD p. 26: “Omnipotence is mediative, therefore the nature saturated in it is regulated and conserved…” Orderliness at every level — atomic nucleus, jeevan’s atma, cosmic regulation — is the same mediative role; that inherent self-regulation gives the darshan its name (slide 22 develops this).

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience
passages.text: Q: Is this a religion or a philosophy? It is presented as a darshan — a way of seeing — offered for study, experiment, and verification in living, not for belief. Its final test is pramanikta: lived evidence in humane conduct. There is no scriptural authority claim, no worship, and no cosmic governor.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience
passages.text: Q: Which texts should I read first? JV is the accessible entry point; SB states the ontology of matter and coexistence most directly; MVD is the systematic darshan text; KD supplies karma, evaluation, and related structure. The study provides page-level citations throughout.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-2
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-2
passages.text: Before the details, here is the map of the argument. One claim — existence is coexistence — moves through three parts.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-2
passages.text: First: what is real, and how it is ordered. There is an all-pervasive ground and countable units, and two bonds — each unit to the ground, and each unit to the others. The second of those is complementarity: each unit stands in definite relations to the rest. Every unit has form, capacities, a way of participating, and an inseparable innateness, expressed across four orders of nature. The darshan connects their inseparability from the ground with its claim that existence neither begins nor ends.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-2
passages.text: Second: how development proceeds along two lines. Composition forms molecules, cells and bodies; material constituents can enter pranic organisation and return to the material order through disintegration. This does not by itself produce a sentient unit. Development in an atom reaches constitutional completeness as jeevan. Across both lines, activity includes effort, motion and result together.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-2
passages.text: Third: how sentient living becomes awakened conduct. We examine the human joint form, jeevan’s faculties and harmonies, evaluation, realisation, and the expression of understanding through humane conduct.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-2
passages.text: Please keep one distinction early: the body line and the sentient-unit line meet in animal and human living, but they are not the same process. That blocks the most common confusion — treating the body as the producer of the knower.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-2
passages.text: Each movement is marked in the small line at the top of its opening slide, so you can always tell where we are.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-2
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-2
passages.text: The three-movement framing is a teaching scaffold for §1, not a separate textual division. Compositional vs atomic development: study §1.6; KD 3.2–3.3. Joint form without identity of process: §1.7; MVD pp. 13, 115.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-2
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-2
passages.text: Q: Why separate the body line from the jeevan line so early? Because the deck will repeatedly use that fork. Bodies compose and decompose; jeevan is constitutional completeness at the atomic level. Collapsing them makes T1 sound like neural complexity and makes death sound like annihilation of the knower.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-2
passages.text: Q: Is this the whole study? No — this deck is §1 (Madhyasth Darshan’s ontology stated on its own terms). Comparison with Advaita, Western philosophy, and science belongs to later sections and a companion session.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-3
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-3
passages.text: Any serious account of reality has to face a small set of questions. Let us name them before we give this tradition’s answers.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-3
passages.text: What is existence? Is there one fundamental reality, or many — and how are they related?

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-3
passages.text: What exists? What are the basic constituents, and what is each of them?

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-3
passages.text: Does what exists begin? Did reality originate at some time — or do only configurations begin and end?

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-3
passages.text: Does the self begin or end with the body?

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-3
passages.text: Is the plural world finally real, or only an appearance?

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-3
passages.text: And sixth: how can what exists be known — what must be understood, and at what scope?

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-3
passages.text: Different traditions answer these differently. Madhyasth Darshan does not answer them with six separate doctrines. One picture — coexistence — is meant to answer all six at once.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-3
passages.text: We will return to this list at the end with the answers filled in. Along the way you will also see how knowing widens, where the developmental drive comes to rest, and how different kinds of evidence are kept distinct.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-3
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-3
passages.text: The study’s framing questions open the paper. Standpoint: from a physics-trained background, consciousness usually appears as something the brain does, yet the hard problem, the status of the self, and the reality of value remain contested — that open space motivates the inquiry.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-3
passages.text: “Humans inherently seek to live with evidence through experimentation, behaviour, and experience…” — SB, p. 44

passages.heading: primary-text-background-3
passages.text: JV, p. 120: justice understood on the basis of relationships; dharma on the basis of orderliness; truth on the basis of existence.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-3
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-3
passages.text: Q: Why is ‘how can it be known?’ an ontological question? Because in MD the way of knowing follows from the way of being: each aspect of a unit demands a definite scope of understanding, and knowledge has an ontological base in orderliness already present in saturated units.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-3
passages.text: Q: Why should we care about ontology — isn’t this abstract? In MD’s reading, complementarity and value are built into existence; justice, family, and undivided society express how reality is — not conventions imposed on a value-neutral world. Slide 27 shows the human goals of resolution, prosperity, fearlessness, and coexistence.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-3
passages.text: Q: How is this different from Vedanta’s answers? Preview only: Advaita answers with Brahman alone and treats the world as mithya at the highest truth. MD keeps both poles real: satta and units are co-eternal, and the world is perpetual (jagat satat). Full contrast is a separate session.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-4
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-4
passages.text: This map is the organising picture for what follows. You do not need to memorise every node. Use it as a place to return when later slides feel dense.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-4
passages.text: At the top: coexistence — the ground and countless units, inseparable without losing their distinction. Then, on the unit side: four aspects of every unit; relationships; four orders of nature; and two developmental lines.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-4
passages.text: Notice the fork. Bodies belong to compositional building. The sentient unit is the result of a different line — development in an atom. The two meet in animal and human living.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-4
passages.text: Later we will name three milestones on the sentient path: the arrival of sentience, then settlement of inner seeking, then authentic conduct. Those are not further material stages.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-4
passages.text: Most of the deck is a zoom into one region of this map.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-4
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-4
passages.text: Companion conceptual map materials under this study folder (SVG/PDF) mirror §1. Primary pointers: MVD, KD, SB, JV as footered on the slide. Two developments and T1–T3: §1.6–§1.6.1; joint form: §1.7; the four classification vocabularies: §1.9.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-4
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-4
passages.text: Q: Is the map itself primary text? No — it is a teaching synthesis of §1. Every node should be checkable against MVD/SB/JV/KD citations developed on later slides.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-4
passages.text: Q: Where do karma and justice sit on this map? Karma (slide 21) structures desire–doing–fruit within sentient activity; regulation and justice (slides 22–23) articulate orderliness and evaluation once the human joint form is in view. They hang off movement 3, not off the ground–unit poles themselves.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-5
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-5
passages.text: We now enter the foundations — what this account says exists.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-5
passages.text: Existence has two inseparable aspects.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-5
passages.text: First, the ground — Omnipresence. Formless, all-pervasive, transparent, permeating, non-transforming, immeasurable. Actionless energy: it acts not at all, yet every unit is energised and regulated in it. There is no place where it is absent.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-5
passages.text: Two words make this relation clearer. Permeating concerns the unit: the pervasive reality passes through every unit, which remains saturated in it. Transparent concerns mutuality: units become manifest to one another through imaging, which provides a basis of recognition. Transparency, permeability, and pervasiveness together evidence one indivisible reality.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-5
passages.text: Second, units of nature. Formful, active, countable. Each is bounded and saturated in the ground. Each has form, capacities, a way of participating, and an inseparable innateness — we will walk those four shortly.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-5
passages.text: Do not collapse levels. At the root, nature is analysed as atomic units — a centre with orbiting parts. Compounds and bodies are composite units. Body and sentient unit together are a joint form. Families and societies are relational assemblies.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-5
passages.text: These two poles were never separate. Separation of a unit from the saturated whole never happens. The ground does not change. Nature saturated in it is dynamic. Therefore all change is unit-activity.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-5
passages.text: One naming caution. The texts list many English names for the ground — including Knowledge and Consciousness. Those names do not mean a mind that knows. Active knowing belongs to the sentient unit, never to the ground.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-5
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-5
passages.text: “Omnipotence is formless and omnipresent. Within Omnipotence, nature is endowed with form, properties, essential nature, and dharma, and is inseparable from it…” — SB, p. 48

passages.heading: primary-text-background-5
passages.text: “Omnipotence remains in a state free from motion and pressure, whereas the whole of nature existing in Omnipotence is present with motion and pressure.” — SB (following p. 48)

passages.heading: primary-text-background-5
passages.text: “The Omnipotence eternally present as omnipresence is an indivisible entity, because its reality is apparent as transparence, permeability and omnipresence.” — SB, p. 46; restated as omnipresent, eternal, ever-existent, transparent, and permeating at SB, p. 160.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-5
passages.text: Source-defined names and translation risks: MVD p. 35 and Editorial Notes in the study. Inter-unit distance held in satta as Space: SB, pp. 57, 59, 79. Never-separated: SB, p. 70; JV, p. 18.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-5
passages.text: MVD p. 32 locates permeation in insentient and sentient units and transparency in their mutuality. PS p. 114 connects this with images and recognition. The ground remains actionless; imaging and recognition do not make it a knowing subject.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-5
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-5
passages.text: Q: Is satta God? “God” is one of the names SB lists — but satta is actionless, formless, and non-willing. MVD’s ninth Reality set: “God is omnipresent, deities are many.” There is no cosmic governor; orderliness is self-regulation.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-5
passages.text: Q: If satta is called Consciousness, is it aware of us? No. “Consciousness” in SB p. 48 labels the all-pervasive reality, not a knowing mind. Sentience as the activity of a knower (chaitanya) is the status of jeevan only.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-5
passages.text: Q: How is satta different from a physical field or the quantum vacuum? A dynamical field carries energy-momentum and propagates waves — unlike actionless, non-transforming satta. Comparisons stay at “consonant with,” never “proved by.”

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-5
passages.text: Q: If units are bounded, what is between them? Not empty in MD’s sense: the distance between bounded wholes is held in formless existence — satta as Space (shunya).

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-6
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-6
passages.text: Saturation names the inseparability of units and Omnipresence. Every formful unit is soaked, submerged, and surrounded in the same pervasive reality.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-6
passages.text: Because that reality is permeating, dividing a unit leaves every fragment saturated in it. There is no fragment outside the ground. This is why the texts connect saturation with non-annihilation, and why saturation names an ever-present condition.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-6
passages.text: The three descriptions have overlapping connections. Soakedness is evidenced as energy-fullness and forcefulness. The unit bears energy and definite relative power. The texts explicitly locate the root of its manifestness, or prakashmanata, in force-endowment while saturated in Omnipresence.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-6
passages.text: Submersion is expressed in activeness and recognition in mutuality. Units are present in the same pervasive reality and are imaged to one another. The formula linking unit-ness and energy-fullness with activeness belongs to this connected account.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-6
passages.text: Surroundedness is evidenced as regulation. Units remain in definite relations and regulate their activities through their own mediative organisation. Slide 22 develops this.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-6
passages.text: These descriptions belong together. The source passages connect them in more than one way, so each card should be read as part of one saturation. Slide 8 develops imaging and recognition. This is the darshan’s ontological account; a quantitative physical mechanism would require further evidence.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-6
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-6
passages.text: The source connects permeability with non-annihilation: “Being soaked itself is forcefulness. It becomes clear that units are soaked because Omnipotence is permeating. No matter how many times we divide a unit, each fragment remains submerged, surrounded, and soaked. It also becomes clear that a unit cannot be annihilated.” — SB, p. 57. Division leaves each fragment saturated; whether this establishes every form of persistence is a further philosophical question. The three aspects taken together, with permeativeness inferred from soakedness: SB, p. 243.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-6
passages.text: Surroundedness as what establishes regulation: “This very surroundedness itself clarifies the regulation of every unit, because every unit … remains regulated within a definite distance from one another, which itself is formless existence.” — SB, p. 79

passages.heading: primary-text-background-6
passages.text: “Every unit in its atomic state is active as orderliness, because it has inherent energy due to being saturated in Omnipotence.” — SB, p. 69

passages.heading: primary-text-background-6
passages.text: “Unit + Energy fullness = Activeness.” — SB, p. 69. The Hindi term is ikaitva, unit-ness — the abstract property of being a bounded unit at all — which the published translation renders as a bare “Unit.” The slide says “unit-ness” for that reason; the study’s glossary carries the same gloss.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-6
passages.text: “Thus, without basic impulsion, the energy remains unmanifest, and without the energy, there is no basic impulsion.” — SB, p. 62

passages.heading: primary-text-background-6
passages.text: Saturation endows forcefulness, basic impulsion, and regulatory order (SB, p. 57). Relative energy does not become apparent without mutuality (MVD, p. 40). Saturation itself as knowledge: MVD, pp. 32–33.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-6
passages.text: SB p. 57 associates soakedness with forcefulness, submersion with activeness, and surroundedness with regulation. PS p. 114 associates soakedness with energy-endowment, submersion with mutual recognition, and surroundedness with regulation. These overlap rather than establishing exclusive compartments. SB p. 248 grounds manifestness in force-endowment under saturation. PS p. 121 identifies the image as a basis of mutual recognition. See study §§1.1–1.3 and Editorial Notes.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-6
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-6
passages.text: Q: Does satta cause unit-activity? Not as an efficient cause. Satta is mahakaran — supreme cause in the sustaining sense (MVD, pp. 288–289; SB, pp. 49, 62). Particular changes occur through unit-activity in mutuality. Slide 7 develops this.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-6
passages.text: Q: Is “inherent energy” measurable physical energy? The texts treat it as ontological endowment. Relative energy appears in unit-mutuality and includes named phenomena such as heat, sound, and electricity. Comparing those terms with measured physical quantities requires a further account; satta’s uniform energy is not thereby identified with a physical field.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-6
passages.text: Q: If complementarity is “given,” why do conflicts exist? Complementarity is perpetual; recognition and fulfilment can fail. At the human order, mis-evaluation under body-identification leaves complementarity incompletely expressed (MVD, p. 112).

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-6
passages.text: Q: Isn’t “a unit cannot be annihilated” contradicted by particle physics? The claim is about what exists, not about the persistence of a particular configuration. Reactions transform arrangements. The study is explicit that this ontological claim is not the same as, and is not proved by, conservation of quantity (§1.14, §6.2).

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-6
passages.text: Q: Does each saturation term have exactly one consequence? The primary descriptions overlap. SB p. 57 connects submersion with activeness, while PS p. 114 connects it with recognition in mutuality. The study preserves both connections and the shared regulation account without assigning one exclusive consequence to each term.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-7
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-7
passages.text: One consequence of the last slide deserves its own moment, because it answers the second of our opening questions.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-7
passages.text: Division leaves every fragment saturated in the ground. Madhyasth Darshan connects this inseparability with its claim that what exists is not annihilated and does not arise from non-being. Existence is perpetual; particular arrangements of units begin and end. The doctrine is explicit, although inseparability alone does not independently prove every claim of persistence.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-7
passages.text: Notice carefully what that does and does not claim. A compound decomposes. A body dies. Those organisations genuinely end. What continues is their constituents, in other relations. Perpetuity belongs to coexistence, not to any particular configuration.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-7
passages.text: Second point, and this one matters for how you hear the rest of the session. The texts call Omnipresence the supreme cause, and that phrase invites a misreading. It is cause only in the sustaining sense — no activity exists apart from nature saturated in it. It starts no particular change. Composition, decomposition, and development occur as unit-activity in mutuality. Karma and humane conduct belong to the human joint form. So there is no creator in this account, and no ruler issuing instructions.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-7
passages.text: Third, time. Time here is not a container existing alongside the ground and the units. Time is the duration of activity, reckoned from recurrent activities — a rotation, a year. The ground does not transform, so it is not temporal in the way unit-activity is measured.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-7
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-7
passages.text: The primary connection between permeability and non-annihilation: “Being soaked itself is forcefulness. It becomes clear that units are soaked because Omnipotence is permeating. No matter how many times we divide a unit, each fragment remains submerged, surrounded, and soaked. It also becomes clear that a unit cannot be annihilated.” — SB, p. 57

passages.heading: primary-text-background-7
passages.text: Perpetuity of existence, and the world’s reality alongside the ground: SB p. 70; JV p. 18. “Brahma is truth, the world is perpetual” — study §1.14, where it is contrasted with the Advaita reading developed in §2.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-7
passages.text: Omnipresence as sustaining rather than efficient cause: SB pp. 48–49; study §1.14. Time as duration of unit-activity: study §1.14, with the full treatment of kaal, trikaalabadh, and spacetime in Nature of Time.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-7
passages.text: The study keeps two claims apart: general indestructibility — nothing existent becomes non-existent — and jeevan’s constitutional completeness (§1.6.1). The second is a further and stronger claim, and is not established by the first.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-7
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-7
passages.text: Q: Doesn’t cosmology say the universe began? Big Bang cosmology describes the evolution of the observable universe from an early hot, dense state. It does not establish creation from non-being; what underlies or precedes that state is open. MD’s claim is about existence as such, not about the age of this configuration. The study takes up the comparison in §4.2 and §6.2.3.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-7
passages.text: Q: What about matter–antimatter annihilation, or a body burning? Both are transformations of configuration, not passage into non-being. MD’s claim concerns what exists, not the survival of particular arrangements. The study is explicit that conservation of quantity alone does not establish MD’s stronger claims.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-7
passages.text: Q: Isn’t this just “energy is conserved” restated? Conservation laws state quantitative relations within physics. MD asserts that what exists does not become non-existent. That stronger ontological claim cannot be derived from conservation laws alone; identifying its units with physical particles would require further argument.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-8
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-8
passages.text: So far the relation I have described runs between each unit and the ground. There is a second relation, and without it nothing else in this account works — not value, not relationship, not justice, and not the drive we are about to follow.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-8
passages.text: Here is where it comes from. Existence is countless units, each with definite limits, in one pervasive reality. That fact — bounded plurality — is itself what makes recognition possible. The text puts it almost casually: “a provision for one unit to recognise another got manifest in existence.” Because there are many bounded things in one ground, each one stands in definite relation to the others.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-8
passages.text: So complementarity is given in coexistence. Not created by us. Not agreed between parties. Not a value we project onto a neutral world. It is a feature of what exists.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-8
passages.text: Three things follow, and they are the three cards.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-8
passages.text: Recognition first. Units are imaged to one another in mutual facing. The image, called pratibimb, provides a basis of mutual recognition. This includes insentient units. Their relative powers also exert effects: heat exchange and particle relations illustrate responsiveness. Imaging and influence have distinct roles in the same mutuality. Neither implies that an insentient unit understands as a person does. Human understanding involves the knowing activities of jeevan.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-8
passages.text: Complementarity second. Nothing in nature exists in isolation, and each unit is a whole along with its environment. Now the consequence people find surprising: value, in the universal sense, is essentiality and participation in orderliness — the definite conduct through which a unit complements others. Usefulness is that essentiality as it appears in objects; it is not the whole of value. Value is ontological here. It is not assigned by an observer, and it is not a human invention layered on top of physics.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-8
passages.text: Fulfilment third. Fulfilment is the participation that follows recognition, according to constitution and order. Below the human order it is definite — it happens. At the human order it must be achieved, through knowing and believing. Which is precisely why, at the human order alone, it can fail.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-8
passages.text: And now the sentence I want you to carry through the rest of the session, because everything from here specifies it: the completeness drive is the drive to fulfil this complementarity. When we get to the composing line, the texts call it a natural inclination toward coexistence. When we get to the sentience threshold, it is hungry atoms and overfull atoms completing each other. When we get to justice, it is complementarity fulfilled knowingly between human beings. Same thing, three registers.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-8
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-8
passages.text: Bounded plurality provisions recognition: “Nature is recognisable in the state-complete Omnipotence with its countless unitness. Consequently, a provision for one unit to recognise another got manifest in existence.” — SB, p. 50; also SB pp. 57, 62.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-8
passages.text: Complementarity given in the bond rather than created: SB pp. 49–50, 53. “Nothing is isolated — that is the principle” — JV, p. 43. “Every entity of nature recognises another; that is why it fulfils…” — JV, p. 69.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-8
passages.text: The equipment of recognition — capacity (kshamata), ability (yogyata), receptivity (patrata): SB pp. 57, 62, 79; MVD p. 62. “Transparent in mutuality”: MVD p. 32.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-8
passages.text: Recognition below the human order is not reflective cognition; the heat, particle-distance, and atomic-combination examples are the study’s own (§1.2). Value as essentiality and participation in orderliness: §1.4.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-8
passages.text: The completeness drive is grounded in these endowments: SB pp. 50–51 — this is the citation behind the closing line of the script. Composition as natural inclination toward coexistence: JV p. 67 (§1.10). Integration at T1 through hungry/undigested (overfull) complementarity: MVD p. 8; SB pp. 58, 71; KD 3.3 (§1.6.1). Justice as recognising relationships, fulfilling values, evaluating the fulfilment, and achieving mutual satisfaction: §1.12.1.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-8
passages.text: PS p. 121 defines image and imaging through mutual recognition. SB pp. 248–252 distinguishes imaging from the influences of relative powers. Its account extends from insentient mutuality to animal recognition of essential nature and human exchange of values and evaluation of dharma. These are the source connections behind the revised study §§1.2–1.3.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-8
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-8
passages.text: Q: Isn’t “complementarity” just cooperation with a nicer name? No — cooperation is something agents choose. Complementarity here is a structural feature of bounded plurality in one ground: it holds between particles that choose nothing. Cooperation, at the human order, is one way of fulfilling it knowingly.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-8
passages.text: Q: If value is built into existence, why do people disagree about values? The claim is that essentiality is objective, not that recognition and evaluation are automatic. Cultures differ in what they recognise and how they evaluate; on this account they are not differing about whether a unit is complementary to others, but about whether they have seen it correctly. The study is explicit that human evaluation can fail (§1.4, §1.12).

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-8
passages.text: Q: Isn’t “recognition” in a particle just a metaphor? The texts give an account of mutual imaging as well as definite responsiveness. PS p. 121 names the image as a basis of recognition, and SB pp. 248–252 distinguishes imaging from influence. Neither attributes human understanding to a particle. Knowing and believing belong to sentient nature (§§1.2–1.3).

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-8
passages.text: Q: How is this different from saying everything is interconnected? “Interconnected” is compatible with the connections being arbitrary or merely causal. The claim here is stronger and more specific: each unit has a definite usefulness to others, given its order and constitution, and that definite usefulness is what value means. Vague holism does not entail an account of justice; this is meant to.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-9
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-9
passages.text: What is every unit? Four inseparable aspects — not a static checklist pasted onto things, but how a definite bearer shows up in the world.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-9
passages.text: Form is the real configuration of the unit: shape, volume, and density. The constituted unit is bimb. Its image in mutual facing is pratibimb, and being imaged is pratibimban. Take the peepal tree: one bounded living form with trunk, branches, leaves, and roots.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-9
passages.text: Properties are relative powers inseparable from their bearer. In the peepal, nutrition, repair, seed production, and degeneration become effective under definite conditions.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-9
passages.text: Essential nature is usefulness in mutuality. The peepal’s effects are vitalising or devitalising according to the affected body and conditions. Its being alive or decomposing does not alone decide which effect it has on another body.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-9
passages.text: Innateness — dharma in this technical sense — is what cannot be separated from the unit, plus order-specific fulfilment. For the peepal: existence plus growth. Seed-conformance is how it conducts itself, not an extra label piled on top.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-9
passages.text: The whole unit is manifest, or prakashman, with all four aspects. Imaging is central to prakash. This is a claim about how units are manifest to one another; completed human understanding also requires knowing their relations and fulfilment. An image alone does not deliver that understanding. Animal recognition of essential nature becomes evident in friendliness and opposition; human living brings the exchange of values and evaluation of dharma.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-9
passages.text: And notice: the tree as a composite can die while its material constituents persist. Persistence of existence is not persistence of one configuration.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-9
passages.text: The same unit is known in three complementary aspects, not three worlds. Inherent truth is what the unit is. Positional truth is how it stands among others. Existential truth is that it exists in Omnipresence.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-9
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-9
passages.text: Four aspects: MVD, pp. 11, 42, 47, 50–51; SB pp. 55, 71, 86. Three complementary truths: YAT; MVD pp. 88, 97; study §1.3. “Each unit is a whole along with its environment… orderliness with its ness… moves towards ‘development’ in its natural state and ‘decline’ in its excited state.” — SB, pp. 13–14

passages.heading: primary-text-background-9
passages.text: Dharma definition and cumulative stack: MVD, pp. 253–254. “Dharma is understood on the basis of ‘orderliness’…” — JV, pp. 120–121. Peepal: JV, p. 113.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-9
passages.text: Editorial Notes: guna and svabhav are relational in manifestation; bearer and capacities remain real.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-9
passages.text: Imaging and prakash: MVD p. 45. Bimb, pratibimb, and pratibimban: PS pp. 121, 135. Being manifest with all four aspects: PS p. 119. Imaging, influence, animal recognition, and human evaluation: SB pp. 248–252. Bearer/property distinction: SB pp. 256–257. SB p. 179 describes entities as manifest, communicated, and expressed according to state, motion, plane, and order. Slide 26 develops the human definitions. The study’s Editorial Notes retain the contextual heated-body definition of prakash in PS p. 119 alongside MVD’s broader imaging formulation.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-9
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-9
passages.text: Q: Isn’t dharma also participation in orderliness? Participation is how dharma is evidenced and understood; inseparability is what dharma is (MVD, pp. 253–254; JV, pp. 120–121).

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-9
passages.text: Q: Is “dharma” here religious duty? No. Unit dharma is ontological innateness and fulfilment. Keep it distinct from the dharma–adharma evaluative perspective on slide 23.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-9
passages.text: Q: How do svabhav and dharma differ? Svabhav is usefulness/essentiality of effects in context; dharma is what cannot be separated from the unit. Caution: MD’s svabhav is not Madhyamaka’s svabhava.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-10
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-10
passages.text: The complementarity we just established becomes evident through relationships among units — this slide is what it looks like in practice.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-10
passages.text: In the material, plant, and animal orders its expression is definite: recognition happens, fulfilment happens. At the human order alone it has to be recognised, evaluated, and fulfilled — so at the human order alone it can be got wrong, and it is got wrong when the body is mistaken for the self.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-10
passages.text: Two kinds of mutuality matter. A relationship carries definite expectations towards completeness — parent and child, for example. In a contact (sampark), the particular exchange is voluntarily undertaken, as when neighbours agree to share the upkeep of a wall. Both remain answerable to justice and humane conduct.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-10
passages.text: The slide names the thirty values: four jeevan values, six human values, nine established values, nine expressed values, and two object values. Established values become evident when human relationships are recognised and fulfilled — trust, respect, affection, care, and so on. Expressed values — shishta-mulya — are their corresponding powers in motion. The English translation of MVD renders those as civic values; they are relationship-expression, not a separate family of right-use of body, mind, and wealth.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-10
passages.text: At the human order the path runs: knowing, then believing, then recognising, then fulfilling. Awakening does not invent new faculties. It aligns this chain with coexistence.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-10
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-10
passages.text: “Every entity of nature recognises another; that is why it fulfils…” — JV, p. 69

passages.heading: primary-text-background-10
passages.text: Relationship / contact definitions: MVD, pp. 61–62. Values and mutuality: SB, pp. 50, 53, 61; MVD, p. 27. Motherly care example: JV, pp. 137–138.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-10
passages.text: The thirty-value enumeration is explicit in Paribhasha Samhita pp. 151, 154; definitions and connections are developed across several passages. Manav Abhyas Darshan, native-reader p. 30, gives the principal nine established values and their paired expressions. The English translation of MVD uses civic values for shishta-mulya; this companion treats them as the expressed pair of the established values. See the study’s §1.4 and Axiology §1.3.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-10
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-10
passages.text: Q: Aren’t values subjective? In MD, essentiality is value — reciprocated and mutually recognised in mutuality. Cultures differ in recognition and evaluation, not in the underlying essentiality.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-10
passages.text: Q: Do relationships exist below the human order? Yes — even physicochemical components recognise and fulfil one another (SB, p. 123). Below the knowledge order, fulfilment is definite; at the human order it must be achieved through the knowing–believing–recognising–fulfilling chain.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-11
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-11
passages.text: Units organise into four stable orders: material; bio or living-plant order; animal; and knowledge — the human order.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-11
passages.text: Read the table downward. Innateness is cumulative. Matter has existence. The bio order adds growth. The animal order adds hope to live. The human order adds happiness. Higher orders include the lower ones.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-11
passages.text: The pivotal boundary is between plant life and animal life. Material and bio orders are non-sentient. Hope to live is where sentience enters. The sentient unit is present in animal and human joint forms.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-11
passages.text: In animals, bodily and brain development limits how much of that unit’s range can be expressed. In humans, the bodily medium can support the full range, but confusion can still misdirect evaluation. Neither body produces sentience. Please do not collapse either case into “mind emerging from matter alone.”

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-11
passages.text: We have now stated what exists and how it is ordered. Next: how development proceeds.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-11
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-11
passages.text: Orders table: SB, p. 179; MVD, pp. 5, 8, 13, 115; JV, p. 44 (six human svabhav qualities). Modes of manifestation per order: MVD, p. 289. Animal adhyasa (gestational inheritance of conduct-pattern): SB, pp. 62–63 — not Advaita’s adhyasa.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-11
passages.text: “Existence is stable and development is definite” — MVD, p. 5.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-11
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-11
passages.text: Q: Where do plants fall? Bio/pranic order — growth added to existence; insentient (no hope to live).

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-11
passages.text: Q: Are animals sentient here? Yes — jeevan first appears at the animal order as joint form. Expression is limited by the bodily medium; awakening to the knowledge order requires the human medium.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-11
passages.text: Q: Is this the same as biological evolution? Overlaps in sequence, differs in modality (niyati-kram vs contingent selection). The study lists this among open problems — be honest.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-12
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-12
passages.text: Start with the question the last three slides have been building toward: why does anything develop at all?

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-12
passages.text: The answer the texts give is the completeness drive. Nature saturated in state-complete Omnipresence is oriented toward development and awakening, until realisation. “Oriented” is doing careful work there — it names a direction inherent in the order of coexistence, not a guarantee that every unit travels the whole way.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-12
passages.text: And here is the connection back to slide 8, which is the one I most want to land: that drive is the drive to fulfil complementarity. Complementarity is given; fulfilling it is what development is. Everything in this movement, and everything in the movement after it, is a specification of that one sentence.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-12
passages.text: That drive proceeds along two distinct lines, and Madhyasth Darshan insists they must not be collapsed.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-12
passages.text: Compositional progression joins particles, atoms, molecules, cells, and bodies into larger configurations. Separately, development in an atom can reach constitutional completeness as a sentient unit. These lines meet in living joint forms, but they remain distinct.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-12
passages.text: Across both, activity is one inseparable triad: effort, motion, and result — three aspects of one activity, not three sequential steps. When sodium and chlorine approach, the approach is effort and motion together; the stable salt crystal is the result.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-12
passages.text: The texts compress the engine this way: saturation is forcefulness; forcefulness is basic impulsion; impulsion is activity; activity is effort-motion-result; and that is development.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-12
passages.text: Each term has a goal: restfulness of effort, destination of motion, immortality of result. Development pervades nature; awakening occurs in the sentient. Non-sentient units participate by composing bodies and environments without each individually completing the drive.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-12
passages.text: The next slide follows both paths through their convergence in animal and human living.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-12
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-12
passages.text: “Every physical-chemical activity is an inseparable presence of effort, motion and result…” — SB, p. 58

passages.heading: primary-text-background-12
passages.text: SB, p. 62 chain; goals: SB, p. 71; MVD, p. 104. Span: SB, pp. 51, 91. Two developments: study §1.6; KD 3.2–3.3.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-12
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-12
passages.text: Q: Isn’t teleology unscientific? Within the system the goals are designed orientations of the triad, not external purposes injected into mechanism. Whether that is defensible against efficient-cause-only physicalism is a comparison question.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-12
passages.text: Q: Is “restfulness of effort” the same as natural-state ease? No. Natural-state ease is insentient complementarity reinstating svabhav gati. Vishram names settlement of internal cognitive effort in jeevan (T2). Do not conflate them.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-13
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-13
passages.text: The completeness drive unfolds along two parallel paths.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-13
passages.text: The first is the compositional path, rachna. Atoms and molecules form material-order structures. Under appropriate chemical and environmental conditions, pranic cells and biological formations appear. This is the material-to-biological order change, and both orders remain insentient.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-13
passages.text: The second is the atomic path, gathan. A developing atom integrates the particle constitution required for completeness. At constitutional completeness, the texts classify that atom as sentient jeevan.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-13
passages.text: The two paths meet in the animal order as a joint form: a biological body plus sentient jeevan. One does not manufacture the other; they work together.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-13
passages.text: Development then continues along both aspects of the joint form. Bodily lineages develop through species-conforming biological organisation, while jeevan’s expression widens through those bodily media. In the animal order that expression remains limited by the body.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-13
passages.text: The human body, in the knowledge order, is described as capable of evidencing all ten activities of jeevan. That does not mean the body owns those activities. It means the bodily medium is adequate for their expression. Once that capacity is present, the remaining development is awakening in jeevan, evidenced through understanding and conduct.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-13
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-13
passages.text: MVD, p. 13 traces chemical and physical composition into biological cells and bodily formations. MVD, p. 26 distinguishes the constitutional-completeness path from compositional formation and identifies human beings as joint forms of insentient and sentient nature.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-13
passages.text: MVD, p. 79 gives the developmental sequence used on the slide. Animal-order bodies are composed of biological cells while the sentient atom advances toward fuller expression. Knowledge-order bodies remain biological compositions, but the human body is capable of evidencing all ten activities of jeevan. The activities belong to jeevan; bodily organisation supplies the medium of expression. MVD, p. 80 restates the categorical distinction: the body is physicochemical composition, while jeevan is the constitutionally complete sentient atom.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-13
passages.text: SB, p. 55 places constitutional completeness in the atom; SB, pp. 76–77 classify material and biological compositions as insentient and animal and knowledge orders as joint expressions. Study §§1.5–1.6, 1.9.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-13
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-13
passages.text: Q: Does development really continue in both body and jeevan in the animal order? Yes, but in different senses. Bodily development is development of species-conforming biological media and lineages. The sentient side advances toward wider expression through those media. The distinction between composition and awakening remains intact.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-13
passages.text: Q: Does the human body possess all ten activities? No. MVD says that the human body is capable of evidencing all ten activities. The activities belong to jeevan; the body is their adequate medium of expression.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-13
passages.text: Q: Are the two paths fused when they meet? No. Animal and human living are joint forms. The biological body remains decomposable, while jeevan is treated as the constitutionally complete sentient unit.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-13
passages.text: Q: Why call the animal order the point of meeting? Because it is the first order described as requiring a joint expression of a biological body and a sentient unit. The material-to-biological transition occurs on the compositional path; the animal order brings that bodily formation into conjunction with jeevan.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-14
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-14
passages.text: Now we name three milestones — T1, T2, and T3.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-14
passages.text: T1 is constitutional completeness: the immortality of result. A developing atom becomes a sentient unit — jeevan. Its standing changes from physicochemical to sentient before realisation, on what the texts call the delusional plane. In human living, delusion means mistaking the body for the self. In animal living, expression is limited by the bodily medium. The plane name should not turn that limitation into a human error or a psychiatric diagnosis.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-14
passages.text: T2 is activity completeness: restfulness of effort. Inner seeking settles into direct realisation and resolution. Status shifts toward awakened understanding.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-14
passages.text: T3 is conduct completeness: destination of motion. Understanding becomes authentic conduct — living proof.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-14
passages.text: Keep T2 and T3 apart. T2 is internal settlement. T3 is outer destination in conduct. And do not confuse T2’s restfulness with the ease of non-sentient natural complementarity.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-14
passages.text: T1 is completeness of an atom’s constitution. T2 and T3 are not further material stages; they name completeness of activity and conduct in the awakened sentient unit. In one line: the saturated realises the ground it is saturated in.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-14
passages.text: One naming point, since I have just used the words. Physicochemical, delusional, deific, divine — the band across the top of this slide — are what the texts call the four planes. A plane is the developmental standing a thing has reached. It is not a kind of thing, and it is not the same as an order of nature. The next slide sorts that out properly.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-14
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-14
passages.text: “In the sentient atom: Conduct completeness is in the form of destination of motion. Activity completeness is in the form of restfulness of effort. Constitutional completeness (the jeevan atom) is in the form of immortality of result.” — SB, p. 58

passages.heading: primary-text-background-14
passages.text: Both MVD and SB use aacharan purnata for T3; vyavahar purnata appears in neither as the T3 term. Plane table: SB, p. 52. Human types by awakening: MVD, p. 160.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-14
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-14
passages.text: Q: Can a transition reverse? T1 is explicitly irreversible at the atomic level (SB, p. 92). For T2/T3 the texts emphasise directional awakening progression rather than a doctrine of relapse.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-14
passages.text: Q: What distinguishes deific from divine? Deific ≈ T2 (understanding settled); divine ≈ T3 (understanding proven in living proof / pramanikta).

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-15
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-15
passages.text: Let me consolidate, because this tradition uses four different vocabularies for what is fundamentally one thing, and mixing them up is the commonest way to get lost in it.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-15
passages.text: There is one drive: nature saturated in state-complete Omnipresence, oriented toward development and awakening until realisation. Everything on this table is a way of describing where something stands in that drive.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-15
passages.text: Orders — material, bio, animal, knowledge — say what kind of thing a unit is: its organisation, its essential nature, its innateness. Four orders.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-15
passages.text: Order and development are described by four terms: existential progression, way of existence, development progression, and awakening progression. The first names the definite order in which the orders become manifest; the second, the conformance by which each order keeps its conduct; the third, physicochemical and atomic development up to T1; the fourth, qualitative development inside a complete sentient unit toward T2 and T3.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-15
passages.text: Planes — physicochemical, delusional, deific, divine — say how far something has come. These are the four we just saw across the top of the last slide. Before T1; T1 only; T2; T3.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-15
passages.text: Human types — animalistic, demonic, humane or discerning, deific, divine — say how a human life is oriented. Five of them, and they classify modes of consciousness and conduct. Not biological species. Not social classes. Not castes.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-15
passages.text: The one caution worth stating out loud: an order is not a plane. The knowledge order spans more than one plane — most human beings are in the knowledge order and on the delusional plane at the same time, and there is nothing insulting in that; it just means realisation has not happened yet. T1 separates physicochemical from sentient standing. T2 and T3 are completeness within an awakened sentient unit, and no fifth plane is added beyond them.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-15
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-15
passages.text: Study §1.6 (the completeness drive), §1.9.1 (terms for order and development), §1.9.2 (four planes, five human types), and the conceptual map’s classification key.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-15
passages.text: The four terms for order and development are niyati-kram (existential progression), niyati-vidhi (way of existence), vikas-kram (development progression), and jagriti-kram (awakening progression): MVD, pp. 13–14; study §1.9.1.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-15
passages.text: The four planes are physicochemical, delusional, deific, and divine or complete: study §1.9.2. Order vs plane asymmetry: SB, p. 52 — two orders can share one plane; one order can span three planes.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-15
passages.text: The five human types are animalistic-human, demonic-human, humane or discerning human, deific-human, and divine-human: MVD, p. 160; study §1.9.2.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-15
passages.text: Note for the presenter: an earlier version of this slide had the plane and progression labels swapped, and listed a set of “planes” (substance, life, intellectual, experiential) that appears nowhere in the study — those are the four orders under another naming. It also ended the human-type list with “transcendental,” which is not a term in this corpus. The table now follows §1.9.1–§1.9.2 exactly. If you have delivered the old version, this is the correction to flag.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-15
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-15
passages.text: Q: Why keep four overlapping vocabularies at all? Because collapsing them produces false equations — “animal order = delusional plane = incomplete atom” is the classic one, and every part of it is wrong. Each vocabulary answers a different question, and the drive they describe is single.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-15
passages.text: Q: Where do the five human types sit? They mark orientation within human living, distributed across planes (MVD, p. 160) — not a fifth ontology beside coexistence, and not a ranking of persons by birth.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-15
passages.text: Q: Is the delusional plane an insult? No, and it is worth saying so. It is the technical name for sentient standing before realisation: the body taken as the self. It names a condition that awakening addresses, not a defect of character. Note also that an animal’s narrower expression is a limitation of its bodily medium, not the specifically human error of body-identification.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-16
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-16
passages.text: This is the claimed sentience threshold. The technical transitions slide names it T1; here the audience-facing question is how the texts say sentience enters.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-16
passages.text: According to the primary texts, sentience appears when one developing atom reaches constitutional completeness — not through neural complexity, molecular size, or the material-to-biological order change.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-16
passages.text: The described process begins with particle exchange. Hungry atoms can incorporate particles; overfull or undigested atoms seek to expel them. Under suitable mutuality, a developing atom integrates the full count required by its constitution. When that requirement is satisfied, the constitution closes and particle count no longer increases or decreases.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-16
passages.text: The slide shows the before and after. Before sentience, the constitution remains open: particles are absorbed or expelled, molecular and weight bondage continue, and kind, capacity, and qualitative change track particle count. At the sentience threshold, all required particles are integrated. The count becomes fixed, molecular and weight bondage end, and qualitative activity continues. The texts classify that closed unit as sentient jeevan.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-16
passages.text: That separation of qualitative from quantitative change is the stated criterion. MVD adds the visible signs of release from the molecular group, liberation from molecular- and weight-bondage, and establishment in hope-bondage.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-16
passages.text: The transition to sentience is therefore a claim of reclassification at atomic closure: one atom becomes jeevan; a body does not become conscious by becoming more complex. The texts give a process and a criterion, but not an accepted physical measurement of this threshold or a causal explanation of why closure is sentience. We will return to that open bridge under method and evidence.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-16
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-16
passages.text: MVD, p. 91 (increased contraction-expansion, release from the molecular group, and the bondage shift). Closed particle constitution: SB, p. 55. Particle inclusion and expulsion as the route to completeness: SB, pp. 58, 71; KD 3.3. Qualitative change tied to quantitative change in matter, and the separation of the two at completeness: SB, p. 86 — this is the criterion stated in the script. Irreversibility: SB, p. 92. Not neural/molecular size: SB, p. 52.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-16
passages.text: Continuity beyond the body and later association with another body: study §1.8, §1.14; JV as cited there. The study keeps this apart from general indestructibility (slide 7): constitutional completeness is MD’s additional reason for identifying jeevan as a persistent individual, not a corollary of quantity conservation.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-16
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-16
passages.text: Q: Is the jeevan atom in the periodic table? No — identifying gathanpurna parmanu with chemistry’s elements is a category error (study).

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-16
passages.text: Q: Can science detect constitutional completeness? Not presently — say so plainly (§6.2.1). Realisation and conduct are warrants within the darshan; public science needs operational criteria that do not yet exist.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-16
passages.text: Q: Does the text explain why closure creates sentience? It identifies closure with the sentient status and describes the before/after criteria. It does not derive sentience from a particle configuration in a way that supplies a contemporary causal model. Calling the sentience threshold a textual transition criterion is more accurate than calling it an empirically established mechanism.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-16
passages.text: Q: Isn’t this just panpsychism? The views differ. Some forms of panpsychism attribute experience to fundamental physical entities; other versions locate it at a wider scale. MD assigns sentience to constitutionally complete atoms. Its pervasive satta is actionless, rather than a collection of minds.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-17
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-17
passages.text: We now turn to human living — movement three.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-17
passages.text: Animal and human living is a joint form. The sentient unit brings the full set of faculties and activities. The body supplies the species-specific medium.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-17
passages.text: On one side: the body — living composition, sense organs, the brain (medhas), physical expression; decomposable. The brain receives and translates signals; it is the medium, not the knower. On the other: the sentient unit — constitutionally complete; faculties inherent; continuing when the joint form ends.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-17
passages.text: Animal bodily development limits expression. The human medium can support the full range, while mistaking the body for the self can still misdirect evaluation.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-17
passages.text: The body gates expression. The sentient unit is seer, doer, and enjoyer through the body. Animal limitation belongs to the medium. Human mis-evaluation belongs to that confusion. The body does not produce sentience, and those two problems are not the same problem.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-17
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-17
passages.text: MVD pp. 13, 115, 288–289; SB pp. 91–92; JV PDF pp. 20, 55 (printed pp. 19, 54). “Jeevan continues to exist even after death as it does while driving a body.” — JV, PDF p. 20

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-17
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-17
passages.text: Q: What is the relationship between jeevan and the brain? The brain (medhas) is a physical interface for expression within the joint form; the knower is always jeevan. How this squares with physical causal closure is an open comparative question the study treats candidly.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-17
passages.text: Q: Do animals have the same jeevan kind? Same kind of constitutionally complete unit; different bodily medium and therefore different expressible range. Full awakening requires the human medium (MVD, p. 115; JV, pp. 79, 93).

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-18
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-18
passages.text: The sentient unit — jeevan — is a constitutionally complete atom.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-18
passages.text: Structurally, atma is the centre. Four faculties surround it: buddhi, chitta, vritti, and mun. The texts distinguish these faculties from their characteristic powers: evidence, resoluteness, desire, thought, and hope.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-18
passages.text: Each characteristic power has outward and inward activities. Mun selects and tastes; vritti analyses and deliberates; chitta visualises and contemplates, including direct apprehension; buddhi resolves and comprehends; atma evidences authenticity and realises. Tasting at mun has three orientations: sensory, value-based, and goal-based. Awakening changes which governs what is accepted. Projection expresses understanding through authenticity, resolve, visualisation, analysis, and selection into living conduct.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-18
passages.text: Here, reflection means pratyavartan, the inward activity of knowing. It differs from pratibimban, the imaging between units introduced on slides 8 and 9. Guidance can descend from the core self through the faculties, while sensory drive can press inward from the body. In awakening, cognisance regulates sensitivity.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-18
passages.text: All five faculties and ten activities belong to the sentient unit. Presence is not the same as expression or effective organisation. Animal bodies limit expression. Humans have the medium for the full range, yet under body-confusion only part of that range may be effectively organised.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-18
passages.text: Study brings understanding. Practice tests and stabilises it. Practice does not manufacture faculties that were missing.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-18
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-18
passages.text: MVD, p. 78; JV, p. 92; MVD, pp. 13, 82–83, 93, 126, 207–208, 278–279, 286–287. Faculties, characteristic powers, and their paired activities: SB p. 63. Atma’s characteristic power, evidence (praman), is distinguished from authenticity (pramanikta) as its projection activity. At the activity level, bal names state and shakti motion; KD §3.8, printed p. 84 supplies the orientation, which the AVD English appendix headings reverse. Body mistaken for self: SB, pp. 91–92; JV, p. 93. The study renders bodh as comprehension and sakshatkar as direct apprehension. Tasting forms: PS pp. 40–41; Axiology §1.2.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-18
passages.text: The koshas in MVD pp. 49–50 describe manifestations across the orders: annamaya/pranamaya already in material nature, manomaya in pranic nature, anandamaya in animal and deluded human living, and vigyanmaya in awakened human living. They are distinct from these five faculties and from the four planes (study §1.5).

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-18
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-18
passages.text: Q: Is atma the same as Vedanta’s Atman? They rhyme but differ: Advaita’s Atman is ultimately identical with one Brahman; MD’s atma is the nucleus of one among countless permanently distinct jeevan units.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-18
passages.text: Q: What does ‘jeevan does not sleep’ mean? Sleep belongs to the body; jeevan’s activities continue. Values and evaluation are jeevan’s practical purpose.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-19
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-19
passages.text: Happiness, peace, contentment, and bliss are not passing moods, and they are not a fourth milestone after T1, T2, and T3.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-19
passages.text: They name harmonies within the sentient unit. Happiness: harmony of hope and thought. Peace: thought and desire. Contentment: desire and resolve. Bliss: resolve and the core self.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-19
passages.text: These four harmonies belong to the knowledge-order account of awakening. Animal living expresses hope to live through its bodily medium. We should therefore keep animal sensory satisfaction distinct from the human development of these harmonies. Within the human account, bliss is borne at buddhi through harmony with atma. Realisation at atma is named ultimate bliss, or paramanand, whose effect reaches the remaining faculties.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-19
passages.text: Their fulfilment is cumulative: resolution; resolution with prosperity; these with fearlessness; and all three in coexistence. Each fuller fulfilment retains the preceding content. These are principal correspondences within one life, not separate compartments or a promise that acquiring goods automatically produces peace.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-19
passages.text: The living cycle is: reflection feeds projection, and projection feeds deeper reflection — that is what living means here. Continuous happiness is harmony evidenced in resolved living, not a sensory spike.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-19
passages.text: The next two slides examine how understanding comes to guide evaluation, work, and relationships.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-19
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-19
passages.text: JV, PDF p. 138 (four harmonies), PDF p. 61 (experienced values and their evidence). KD §3.12, printed p. 112 gives cumulative fulfilment; pp. 110–113 develops projection–reflection. SB pairs values with practical routes through justice, orderliness, and realisation. MVD, p. 77 (channelling energies toward awakening).

passages.heading: primary-text-background-19
passages.text: Study §1.8 locates happiness at mun, peace at vritti, contentment at chitta, and bliss at buddhi, each through harmony with the inward faculty. MVD pp. 100–101 distinguishes ultimate bliss at realised atma; MVD pp. 328–346 enumerates the faculty activities. The knowledge-order ladder should not be extended to animals merely from the presence of the same faculties.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-19
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-19
passages.text: Q: Are these only for the fully awakened? They register progressively — milestones of awakening, not a distant prize (JV, p. 61).

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-19
passages.text: Q: Why can’t sensory pleasure provide continuous happiness? Comforts and accumulation aim at happiness but carry momentariness and fragility (AVD). Continuity is harmony within jeevan.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-20
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-20
passages.text: Every sentient unit bears the same five faculties and the same ten activities. What differs is the medium and what the unit does with it.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-20
