passages.text: Take the animal case first. An animal jeevan has all five faculties, but its bodily medium limits their expression. Its dharma is hope to live, expressed through sensory selection under species-conformance. The human medium supports the full range of activity and the possibility of awakening.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-20
passages.text: Now the human case. The human body can express all ten activities — that is what the developed nervous system is for. And yet, by default, human jeevan goes on evaluating by exactly the same sensory criteria the animal used. The equipment changed; the habit did not. That is the fork this slide names, and it answers one practical question — what makes me happy?

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-20
passages.text: Under confusion, the body is mistaken for the self. Selection and evaluation organise around pleasure, health, and profit.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-20
passages.text: Under awakening, clear knowing regulates sensory life. Knowing and believing guide recognition and fulfilment toward justice, innateness, truth, and coexistence.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-20
passages.text: No faculty is missing, and sensation is not rejected. Confusion lets sensory criteria rule; awakening balances sensation with understanding, so understanding guides conduct.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-20
passages.text: When the same fork is resolved in a person and sustained across a tradition, it shows as resolution, prosperity, fearlessness, and coexistence.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-20
passages.text: Awakening requires more than preferring the right things or having an insight that does not guide conduct. The next slide explains how understanding becomes effective in living.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-20
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-20
passages.text: SB, p. 64 (cognisance–sensitivity balance); JV, pp. 73–74, 92–94 (four-and-a-half activities); MVD, pp. 274–275; study §§1.7–1.8, 1.10, 1.12, 1.15.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-20
passages.text: The animal case: hope to live is the animal-order dharma, expressed through mun; the animal body provides for hope-bound, species-conformant expression without providing for the complete evidence of understanding (study §§1.5, 1.7). The four-and-a-half activities organised around bodily sensitivity in deluded human living: study §1.7; JV, pp. 73–74, 92–94.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-20
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-20
passages.text: Q: Is delusion moral blame? It is a developmental and evaluative condition — body mistaken for self — not an insult. The remedy path is study, practice, and realisation, not shaming.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-20
passages.text: Q: Can someone be partly awake? Awakening progression is graded (planes and human types). The slide’s fork names the organising refuge, not a binary personality test.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-21
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-21
passages.text: So: peace, contentment, bliss. How does a person actually get them?

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-21
passages.text: Let me put the shape of the answer first, because it is the hinge of this whole movement. Below the human order, fulfilment is definite — it needs no deciding. A molecule does not choose. A plant does not deliberate. Even the animal, which has a complete sentient unit, is carried by species-conformance to the fulfilment available through its body. Nothing there has to be worked out.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-21
passages.text: The human order is the one place where complementarity has to be fulfilled knowingly — where the higher harmonies are on offer and nothing delivers them automatically. Study introduces the account; understanding must become coherent activity. Knowing is itself an activity of jeevan, and its authenticity is evidenced in work and behaviour. Book knowledge alone does not establish that completed coherence.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-21
passages.text: Understanding is evidenced as relationships are fulfilled. We study, practise, evaluate the result, and bring work and behaviour into alignment with what we understand. The harmony within jeevan and its evidence in living belong together.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-21
passages.text: That is why the text bothers with the anatomy of action at all. Kriyā names activity throughout nature; it is not thereby karma. Human activity joined to aspiration has five limbs: doer, cause, objective, result, and effect. Effect means the act’s reach or consequence — not a separate ledger of destiny. Desire is the aspiration; karma is the doing, activity together with aspiration; result is the fruit. And the text’s own criterion: desire, doing, and result must balance for the desire to be truly accomplished. Wanting without doing is not accomplishment. Doing that misses the result is not accomplishment either.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-21
passages.text: The intended result is accomplished through doing. Understanding guides that doing, and its authenticity is evidenced in conduct that fulfils relationships.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-21
passages.text: Hold this beside the earlier triad of effort, motion, and result. This is the desire-laden human framing of the same activity ontology. The next slides show how desire and doing get reorganised under justice, innateness, and truth.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-21
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-21
passages.text: “Activity together with aspiration is karma itself … it is the balance of desire, karma, and result that is the accomplishment of the desire.” — KD Ch. 1, pp. 1–2

passages.heading: primary-text-background-21
passages.text: Five limbs as on the slide. Relate to effort–motion–result (slide 12) without collapsing the vocabularies — kriyā names activity throughout nature, while karma names human activity together with aspiration.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-21
passages.text: Why this slide sits here: the four harmonies are jeevan values (study §1.8), and the study is explicit that they correspond to widening fields of evidence — resolution in the person, peace tested in family prosperity, contentment in fearless social participation, bliss in the living and communicating of coexistence. Evidence requires projection, and projection is conduct. Hence KD’s insistence that book knowledge is not the completion of the process: “Study, practice, work, behaviour, result, and purpose must become coherent” (study §1.8). Definite fulfilment below the human order: study §§1.4, 1.11 — recognition and fulfilment are definite according to structural, seed, and species conformance.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-21
passages.text: Also relevant: “Living proof requires understanding to become conduct; insight that does not regulate action has not completed the projection–reflection cycle” (study §1.7.1).

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-21
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-21
passages.text: Q: Is this karmic cosmology with rebirth accounting? KD here analyses the structure of intentional activity. Post-body continuity is argued from T1 elsewhere; do not smuggle a popular karma-punishment story into this slide.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-21
passages.text: Q: How does this relate to effort–motion–result? Same underlying activity ontology; karma names human activity-with-aspiration and its fruit in the desire register. Keep the five limbs available for Q&A on responsibility and result.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-21
passages.text: Q: If action is what matters, why spend so long on the ontology? Because action without truthful understanding reproduces the confusion it came from — the study’s phrase is that projection without truthful understanding can reproduce delusion (§1.6.3). The claim is not that study is unnecessary. It is that study is half. Reflection without projection remains unevidenced; projection without reflection goes wrong.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-21
passages.text: Q: Can’t I just be a good person without any of this? Good conduct is valuable, but conduct completeness means the individual’s continuous expression of realised understanding. MVD pp. 15–16 distinguishes completeness in an individual from completeness in society. A person’s humane participation helps establish and transmit an awakened tradition; it does not require an already completed universal society. The claim is assessed through understanding, fulfilled relationships and continuity of conduct (§1.6.3, §1.15).

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-22
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-22
passages.text: This slide explains the name Madhyasth — and it cashes a cheque I wrote back on slide 6.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-22
passages.text: Remember the third of the three terms: surrounded. Regulation is what surroundedness establishes. Because the formless reality stands between units, each is held at a definite distance from the others. Orderliness is self-regulation inherent in saturated units — not dispensed by a cosmic governor. That mediative regulation, which regulates and conserves every unit, gives the darshan its name.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-22
passages.text: The account works at three levels, and it is worth naming them: Omnipresence is the sustaining condition; within an atom, the nucleus is the mediative organisation that regulates generative and degenerative activity and conserves relative powers; and at larger scales, order-specific conformance is the definite conduct you can actually observe.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-22
passages.text: Conformance has order-specific modes. Material: structural or result conformance. Bio: seed-conformance. Animal: species-conformance, inherited from gestation. Human: sanskar-conformance — conduct follows acquired acceptances and dispositions. These can express delusion or awakened understanding. That is why education and tradition matter: they can reproduce confusion or support awakening.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-22
passages.text: Material, bio, and animal regulation is definite. An animal body’s expressive limits do not introduce evaluative error. In human living, the sentient unit can judge wrongly when it mistakes the body for the self. Awakening aligns evaluation with coexistence. That is why justice becomes necessary at the human order.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-22
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-22
passages.text: “Regulation itself becomes clear in the form of law…” — SB, p. 57

passages.heading: primary-text-background-22
passages.text: “Omnipotence is mediative, therefore the nature saturated in it is regulated and conserved…” — MVD, p. 26

passages.heading: primary-text-background-22
passages.text: Surroundedness as the specific ground of regulation: “This very surroundedness itself clarifies the regulation of every unit, because every unit … remains regulated within a definite distance from one another, which itself is formless existence.” — SB, p. 79

passages.heading: primary-text-background-22
passages.text: Human conformance is sanskar-conformance in the study’s table (§1.11); human bodily composition remains species-conformant, but human conduct is principally jeevan-based and sanskar-conformant. The three levels of the account — sustaining condition, mediative nucleus, order-specific conformance — are set out in §1.11.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-22
passages.text: KD, p. 14 (law across family, nation, world). Justice definition reserved for next slides: MVD, p. 311.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-22
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-22
passages.text: Q: If there’s no cosmic enforcer, why do units obey law? Law is the form regulation takes in saturated units — provisioned from within. Below the human order, conformance cannot fail; at the human order it must be achieved.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-22
passages.text: Q: Is animal limitation the same as human error? No — animals have definite fulfilment with limited expression; humans can mis-evaluate under body-delusion. That is why justice becomes necessary at the knowledge order.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-23
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-23
passages.text: Human evaluation widens across six perspectives: pleasant, healthy, profit, justice, innateness or dharma as an evaluative lens, and truth. They move from sensation, body, and gain to relationship, orderliness, and coexistence.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-23
passages.text: Justice is both one of the six and the principle of fulfilled relationship. Dharma here means fitting the wider pattern — discipline in thought, not only outer conduct. Truth means alignment with the whole, grounded in realisation, not in liking or gain.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-23
passages.text: The graduated chain is: rule itself is justice; justice itself is dharma; dharma itself is truth; truth itself is coexistence.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-23
passages.text: Pleasure, health, and profit are not condemned. They remain legitimate in their domain. Awakening changes the organising refuge: they are subordinated under justice, dharma, and truth — not abandoned.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-23
passages.text: Keep this distinct from unit-innateness earlier. One word, two levels: what a unit cannot be separated from, versus how we evaluate thought and resolution.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-23
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-23
passages.text: KD, pp. 10, 13, 60, 86; study §1.12–§1.12.1. MVD, p. 67 (six perspectives); MVD, p. 137 (justice regulates behaviour, dharma disciplines thought, realisation only through truth); MVD, p. 311 (justice as recognising relationships, fulfilling values, evaluating, mutual satisfaction). JV, pp. 138–139 (deliberation bases).

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-23
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-23
passages.text: Q: Are pleasure, health, and profit condemned? No — legitimate in their domain; awakening changes the organising refuge.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-23
passages.text: Q: How does this relate to courts? Distinguish inherent regulation, justice as relational closure, and statutory law. Statute can be legal and unjust.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-24
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-24
passages.text: We turn now to knowing — how understanding widens, and how it happens in the sentient unit.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-24
passages.text: On the left: what must be understood as mutual context widens. Form is real structure encountered in mutual facing. Capacities show as effects between units. Essential nature needs state, order, and context. Innateness is evidenced in whole-order fulfilment. Relationships are shared expectations weighed by justice, dharma, and truth. At the top is coexistence itself — not another observed detail, but the aim of knowing.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-24
passages.text: On the right: how knowing happens within the sentient unit. Mun tastes and selects. Vritti deliberates. Chitta contemplates and directly apprehends. Buddhi comprehends and resolves. Atma realises in truth. Happiness, peace, contentment, and bliss name harmonies between paired faculties. Realisation at atma is named ultimate bliss.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-24
passages.text: Every unit is already manifest with all four aspects. The left-hand steps describe widening human understanding of that unit; they do not describe successive additions to its image. Inward reflection deepens knowing, and projection makes understanding evident through conduct. Bliss names the harmony of buddhi and atma; coexistence realised at atma is ultimate bliss.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-24
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-24
passages.text: JV, p. 120 (triad epistemic bases); JV, p. 121; SB, p. 50 (ultimate dharma); JV, p. 120 (understanding of existence, jeevan, and humane conduct); MVD, pp. 78, 101, 137; JV, p. 61; study §§1.3–1.4, 1.7–1.13.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-24
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-24
passages.text: Q: Why is dharma on the top rung when atma is at the centre of the atom diagram? Different geometries: atom diagram is structural (inward = deeper); ladder is epistemic (higher = wider context needed). All four aspects are equally present in every unit.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-24
passages.text: Q: Is this ladder stated verbatim in the texts? The ladder is an analytical arrangement of the definitions and their contexts, as explained in the study. All four aspects belong to the manifest unit. Imaging supplies a basis of recognition, while human understanding develops through jeevan’s knowing activities; the rungs should not be taught as a source-enumerated sequence of images.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-25
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-25
passages.text: This is where the developmental drive comes to rest: realisation in coexistence.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-25
passages.text: The drive settles when relationships across nature are fulfilled and made evident — not because the ground becomes a knower, but because the awakened sentient unit realises and evidences the coexistence in which it has always existed.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-25
passages.text: Realisation at atma is named ultimate bliss. Bliss names the harmony of buddhi and atma. What is known is existence as coexistence: nature saturated in Omnipresence. Understanding becomes evident as authenticity in work, behaviour, and participation. The next slide examines how it is presented, communicated, and expressed.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-25
passages.text: Three roles stay distinct: the sentient unit remains the knower; existence as coexistence remains the known; knowledge becomes evident as authentic conduct. They become coherent without becoming identical. The individual knower is not dissolved into a single universal Self.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-25
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-25
passages.text: “The goal of development is for nature, saturated in Omnipotence, to be realised in Omnipotence…” — SB, p. 81

passages.heading: primary-text-background-25
passages.text: SB, p. 116 and MVD, p. 126 (threefold knowledge); KD §§3.17–3.18 (knowledge, knower, and known); MVD, pp. 14–15, 286–287. Study §1.13.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-25
passages.text: MVD pp. 100–101 distinguishes ultimate bliss at atma; MVD p. 328 connects realisation-based expression, communication, and exposition with ultimate bliss. Study §§1.8 and 1.13 preserves both this placement and bliss as buddhi–atma harmony.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-25
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-25
passages.text: Q: If satta is Knowledge, doesn’t it know everything? No — gyan as satta names intelligibility, not cognition. The knowing act belongs only to jeevan.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-25
passages.text: Q: How is this different from moksha as merger? MD denies merger into a single Self. Realisation evidences coexistence; individuality of jeevan remains ontologically real.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-26
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-26
passages.text: How does understanding become available in living? The primary texts use three connected terms: presentation, communication, and expression.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-26
passages.text: Presentation, prakashan, makes actuality evident through an accomplished and meaningful form. Something understood takes a form another can attend to.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-26
passages.text: Communication, sampreshana, indicates completeness. The definition names constitutional completeness, activity completeness, and conduct completeness. Communication serves understanding and enabling another to understand. Words direct attention to the activity of units and its inherent meaning, including their properties, essential nature, and dharma.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-26
passages.text: Expression, abhivyakti, is the mental, verbal, and bodily activity through which our existence is evidenced for all-round resolution, called abhyudaya. Understanding is expressed in speech, work, and humane behaviour.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-26
passages.text: Art, kala, concerns how these activities take an accomplished form. It makes qualities evident and expression meaningful, bringing usefulness together with beauty. In making an object, art value enhances usefulness. In communicating understanding, art serves intelligibility and the purpose of resolution.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-26
passages.text: These activities belong together in the participation of jeevan through the body. They carry understanding into the awakened human tradition on the next slide.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-26
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-26
passages.text: The general scope is unit expression according to state, motion, developmental plane, and order (SB p. 179), and all units’ expressions as activity saturated in Omnipresence (MVD p. 109). The human definitions are PS p. 119 for prakashan, p. 206 for sampreshana, and p. 22 for abhivyakti. The definition of abhivyakti itself includes prakashan and the participation of hope, thought, desire, resolve, experience, and bodily activity.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-26
passages.text: MVD pp. 109–110 connects form activity, word activity, inherent meaning, and communication as understanding and enabling understanding. MVD p. 328 brings realisation-based expression, communication, and exposition together under ultimate bliss. These connections support a coherent account without assigning each term exclusively to one faculty pair.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-26
passages.text: PS p. 56 defines kala through making qualities evident and expression meaningful, and the joint accomplishment of usefulness and beauty. Its object-value application, kala-mulya, concerns enhancing usefulness; the general definition also concerns communication and conduct. All PS page numbers are printed pages in the edition identified at the start of this companion. Study §1.13 and Editorial Notes give the connected reading and contextual qualifications.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-26
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-26
passages.text: Q: Does each term add a new layer to the unit’s image? The sources do not establish three successive layers or an exhaustive partition of manifestness. The terms overlap, and abhivyakti’s definition includes prakashan. Their human definitions specify meaningful presentation, indication of completeness, and expression for all-round resolution.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-26
passages.text: Q: Can we map presentation to vritti–chitta, communication to chitta–buddhi, and expression to buddhi–atma? The reviewed definitions do not establish that exclusive assignment. MVD p. 328 uses all three together for realisation-based ultimate bliss, and abhivyakti involves the full activity of jeevan through the body. The faculty harmonies on slide 19 remain distinct definitions.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-26
passages.text: Q: Does kala mean decoration? Its definition joins usefulness and beauty and makes expression meaningful. A clear explanation or accomplished piece of work can evidence it. Object art value is one application of this broader account.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-27
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-27
passages.text: Conduct completeness is realised understanding expressed continuously by the individual. Humane participation and education transmit it through an awakened tradition. Individual completeness contributes to social completeness; it does not wait for the entire society to be complete.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-27
passages.text: Effort settled in realisation is T2. Understanding proven in conduct is T3.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-27
passages.text: Four goals at four levels: resolution in every person; prosperity in every family; fearlessness — trust — in society; coexistence with all of nature.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-27
passages.text: Five social systems carry that continuity: education and formative culture; justice and preservation; health and restraint; production and work; exchange and storage. These differ from the four dimensions of a person’s living — realisation, thought, behaviour and work.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-27
passages.text: And here is where the other half of the composition slide returns. Families and societies are not a further compositional tier — you cannot get a humane society by stacking bodies the way you stack molecules. They are relational achievements: they persist humanely while relationships are recognised, values fulfilled, evaluation completed, and mutual satisfaction achieved. Fear, force, or extraction can hold a group together for a while; on this account they do not make it an orderly society.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-27
passages.text: MD connects this social aim with human dharma as happiness, values fulfilled in relationships, and understanding expressed in conduct. Nature is oriented towards development and realisation; an awakened human tradition requires people to understand, practise, and transmit that understanding. The ontology gives this participation a purpose without making humane institutions automatic.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-27
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-27
passages.text: JV, PDF p. 61; MVD, pp. 13–16; SB, pp. 51, 81, 91. Individual and social completeness are distinguished in MVD pp. 15–16. Five social systems: study §1.15 and governance-related works in the series. SB on operating scale of self-sustaining systems (100–200 families) if useful for Q&A.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-27
passages.text: Human assemblies as achieved rather than chemically definite: study §1.10, final paragraph; MVD, p. 42; SB, p. 14 (persist or decline). This is the counterpart of slide 13 — the compositional half of §1.10 was delivered there, the relational half here.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-27
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-27
passages.text: Q: Isn’t ‘producing more than needed’ just growth ideology? No — samridhi is felt sufficiency with proper utilisation, opposed to hoarding (AVD).

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-27
passages.text: Q: How does family-scale vision reach society? Through coordinated participation in recognised relationships, expressed institutionally across the five social systems. Social continuity requires continued fulfilment; it is not a chemical composition of persons.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-28
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-28
passages.text: Before the closing summary, I owe you an accounting of what kind of thing each part of this has been.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-28
passages.text: Different methods establish different things. They can support one another, but they are not interchangeable.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-28
passages.text: Logical exposition can show internal coherence. It cannot by itself prove empirical fact.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-28
passages.text: Study and self-examination can show intelligibility and first-person recognition. They cannot by themselves physically identify the sentient unit.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-28
passages.text: Practice and conduct-evidence can show effects in work, behaviour, and mutual satisfaction. They cannot by themselves measure the sentience threshold or the unit–body interface.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-28
passages.text: Realisation is this tradition’s claimed completion of knowing. It does not force agreement from other methods.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-28
passages.text: Publicly measurable physical claims remain answerable to instrument-based science. No accepted measurement currently identifies the sentience threshold, the unit–body interface, or post-body reassociation — the last of those being the claim I flagged on slide 16, that the sentient unit continues when a body ends and may later associate with another. Stating that plainly is part of responsible presentation.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-28
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-28
passages.text: Study §1.15–§1.16. Staged method from MVD, p. 88 and SB, p. 44: study → experiment and practice → realisation with evidence. Open problems: study §§6.1–6.2.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-28
passages.text: Note on placement: this slide now sits immediately before the closing summary, so the honesty about warrant lands as the last word on method rather than interrupting the ascent through realisation and tradition. Every claim it names as unmeasured has actually been made earlier in the deck — T1 on slide 16, the interface on slide 17, reassociation on slide 16 — so nothing here is a caveat about a claim the audience has not heard.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-28
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-28
passages.text: Q: Has any of this been proven scientifically? Be precise: internal coherence and conceptual consonance are not instrument confirmation of T1 or post-body continuity. Use “consonant with,” never “supported by,” without evidence.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-28
passages.text: Q: Then why present it? Because ontology can still be examined for definitions, entailments, and lived testability — and because refusing to overclaim is part of the method.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-29
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-29
passages.text: Let us close the loop on the six questions.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-29
passages.text: What is existence? Eternal coexistence: countless units saturated in all-pervasive Omnipresence.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-29
passages.text: What exists? Root atomic units; composite units and bodies; body–sentient-unit joint forms; and relational human assemblies — all saturated in the ground.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-29
passages.text: Does existence begin or end? No. Existence is perpetual. Configurations form, transform, and decompose.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-29
passages.text: What is the self? The constitutionally complete sentient unit working through the body.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-29
passages.text: Is the world real? Yes. Units, mutual relationships, and definite material fulfilment are real within perpetual coexistence.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-29
passages.text: How is it known? Through logical exposition, study and self-examination, practice, realisation, and conduct-evidence — without conflating those with instrument measurement of the sentience threshold. The lived test is evidence in humane conduct.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-29
passages.text: If we continue later, the natural next step is comparison with other traditions and with science — including open problems this study names for Madhyasth Darshan itself. Thank you.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-29
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-29
passages.text: Study §1.16 table. Staged method: MVD, p. 88; SB, p. 44. Open problems: §§6.1–6.2 (latency reading, conservation-to-immortality inference, jeevan–body interaction, operationalization of T1, niyati-kram vs evolution).

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-29
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-29
passages.text: Q: Where should someone start? Follow the staging: study (JV, then SB/MVD with this paper as map) → experiment and practice in living → let realisation and conduct be the test. Jeevan Vidya shivirs follow this format.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-29
passages.text: Q: What’s the single takeaway? Existence is coexistence: a changeless, actionless ground and countless real units, saturated together — and because complementarity and value are built into that togetherness, human fulfilment is recognising and fulfilling relationships, evidenced in conduct. Resolution = happiness.
